page: Amazon Web Services inf1.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System, engineered specifically for machine learning inference applications. It features 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory is configured with 8.0 GB of DDR4 system RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is supplied by a single AWS Inferentia chip equipped with 8 GB of dedicated accelerator memory. The instance does not include bundled local storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal that general host computing performance is modest. The system recorded a multi-core score of 3929.66 on stress-ng and 2526.0 on Geekbench multi-core tests, placing general CPU throughput in lower percentiles. The PassMark CPU score of 4625.12 reflects its allocation of two physical hyperthreaded cores. Evaluated on small 135M language models, prompt processing registered 225.83 tokens per second, while text generation reached 75.74 tokens per second, falling within the middle tier for generation. Memory bandwidth benchmarks yielded 27.68 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 23.83 GB/sec for uncached writes.

Because host CPU compute and general-purpose memory bandwidth are conservative, running general application logic or compute-heavy host transformations on inf1.xlarge involves notable performance tradeoffs. In terms of cost efficiency, the hardware configuration is economically structured for specialized deployment pipelines where inference models fit within the dedicated 8 GB Inferentia accelerator memory rather than relying on expensive multi-purpose GPU configurations.

Amazon Web Services inf1.xlarge is best suited for targeted machine learning inference workloads, including natural language processing, text generation, sentiment analysis, and image classification models optimized specifically for AWS Inferentia processors.
description: Amazon Web Services inf1.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor, designed for machine learning inference. The host platform provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, supported by 8.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. Hardware acceleration is delivered by a dedicated AWS Inferentia chip with 8 GB of VRAM. The instance features no local storage and maintains a 5 Gbps baseline network throughput. Synthetic benchmarks show conservative general-purpose CPU and memory metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 2526.0 and stress-ng multi-core result of 3929.66. In LLM benchmarks using a 135M model, it achieved 75.74 tokens per second in text generation. The inf1.xlarge instance provides an economical hardware profile for serving trained machine learning models, natural language processing tasks, and inference microservices without the overhead of heavy-duty general compute platforms.
